name: Banh Mi Panzanella

instructions.primary_message: For the Tofu: Transfer tofu to a large zipper-lock freezer bag. In a small bowl, whisk together lemongrass, soy sauce, honey, and fish sauce. Pour marinade over tofu, press out all air from the bag, seal, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or overnight, turning once halfway through marinating time.
Drain tofu and pat dry with paper towels. In a large nonstick skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add tofu and cook, turning, until crispy. Set aside.
Meanwhile, for the Hoisin-Honey Sauce: In a medium bowl, whisk together hoisin, rice wine vinegar, honey, sesame oil, and soy sauce. Set aside or refrigerate until ready to use.
For the Chili Mayo: In a medium bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, Sriracha, and rice wine vinegar. Set aside or refrigerate until ready to use.

For the Salad: In a large bowl, combine tofu, bread, cucumber, jalapeños, cilantro, and drained pickled vegetables. Drizzle with hoisin-honey sauce and toss again to coat. Transfer salad to serving plate, drizzle with chili mayo and serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: Asian, bánh mì, bread, panzanella, salad, tofu

description: The classic flavors of Vietnamese banh mi sandwiches are reworked into the form of Italian panzanella, a salad designed to make stale bread delicious again. This version features pickled and fresh vegetables, lemongrass-marinated tofu, and two sauces that deliver spicy, sweet, and savory flavors.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 50 min to 10 hr 20 min.

Optional substitutions: vegetable oil → canola oil

Notes: To dry tofu, line a rimmed baking sheet with paper towels. Place tofu cubes on top in a single layer. Cover with another layer of paper towels and press gently to remove excess moisture. If using fresh bread instead of stale, cut into cubes and bake at 300°F until firm and lightly browned, about 20 minutes.
author: Morgan Eisenberg
